title: A Static for the Gravity Anew
premise: Wren Nystrom, a clone of a murdered courier, hauls cargo along the silent corridor between the cryo-arks of Meridian and the orbital habitats of Halcyon, carrying the unsolved case file of the man he was copied from. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Wren discovers the flicker was a signal from a faction inside Halcyon that can only wake one ark's worth of sleepers before power collapses entirely. As he investigates his original's murder, he finds the killer is alive, powerful, and now deciding who wakes — and that his own cloned memories hold the evidence to stop them. In the end, Wren sacrifices his claim to personhood by broadcasting his original's testimony under the dead man's name, waking both arks at half-strength and choosing belonging over justice for himself.
about_author: Ivo Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that rarely spoke directly. They write about distance, duty, and the people who keep signals alive between worlds.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Wren runs the supply line between silent Meridian and Halcyon, logging the monotony of a route no one thanks him for. Through his POV we learn he's a clone living on a dead man's license, haunted by fragments of memory that aren't his. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Gravity fails across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; Wren's ship drifts into a debris field and he barely survives. A hidden transmission embedded in the flicker resolves into coordinates — and a voice using his original's cadence. Emotional beat: terror giving way to the vertigo of being chosen.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Evidence
chapters.summary: Following the coordinates, Wren opens a cache his original hid before dying: logs proving Halcyon's Wake Authority has been siphoning ark power for decades. His cloned memories begin unlocking in response to the files. Emotional beat: the uncanny intimacy of reading your own handwriting from a life you never lived.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Signed the Order
chapters.summary: On Halcyon, Wren meets Director Sefa Okonkwo-Vale, who knew his original — perhaps loved him — and who now controls which half of humanity wakes. She offers Wren legitimacy, a name, a place. Her POV reveals she believes she is saving civilization, not corrupting it. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's unlocked memories surface the night of the original's murder: an argument with Sefa over the ark power diversion. He can't tell what he witnessed and what he invented. He tests his memories against physical records and they hold. Emotional beat: self-doubt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Meridian Answers
chapters.summary: Wren risks the silent corridor to reach Meridian's ark, where engineer Tovi Reyes has been keeping the sleepers alive off-grid. Tovi confirms the power math: only one ark can wake fully. Tovi's POV shows the quiet heroism of custodianship. Emotional beat: finding family in strangers who share your duty.

chapters.title: A Murder Reopened
chapters.summary: Sefa learns Wren has the cache and moves to seize it, framing him as a malfunctioning copy with no legal standing. Wren is detained aboard Halcyon while the Wake countdown accelerates. Emotional beat: betrayal — the belonging offered was always conditional.

chapters.title: The Testimony of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Tovi smuggles Wren's broadcast rig into the detention block. Wren realizes the only testimony with legal force belongs to his original — so he compiles the evidence under the dead man's identity, erasing himself as its author. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Gravity, Restored
chapters.summary: The testimony goes out during the second flicker, forcing open hearings as systems fail. Sefa, confronted by her own recorded words, stands down rather than become the thing she fought. The compromise is brutal but real: both arks wake at half capacity. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph.

chapters.title: A Static for the Gravity Anew
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wren runs the route again — but now both worlds speak, and Tovi rides shotgun. He registers under his own name, first of his line, carrying the original's memory as inheritance rather than burden. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; belonging earned, not granted.
